cases.note: Zig errors NotAKey, DuplicateKey. An item's "key" is the item itself; the splice overwrote its value. YAML's parser accepts the repeat, so the engine is the net: by name up front, and by count from key syntax. Its own name is not a repeat, and a new one lands. The Zig test also checks the editor's internal `splice_rejected` flag, which a fixture cannot see. Its `replaceKeyAtPath` steps (key syntax, checked by count after the splice) are the binding's by-name `renameKey`, checked up front.

cases.id: insertValue rolls back an insert that repeats a name, from key syntax
cases.note: Zig error DuplicateKey. A document that already repeats a name is not refused an unrelated insert — only an insert that adds a repeat is. The Zig test passes key syntax (`insertKey`), where only the reparse knows the name; the binding inserts by name (`insertValue`), so these steps hold the same refusals through the up-front name check.

cases.id: set reports the flow container, not a missing key, when a block value can't land
cases.note: Zig error BlockValueIntoFlow. The parent exists and IS a mapping — just a flow one. Falling back to the replace branch's `NotFound` would send the caller after a key that isn't the problem.

cases.id: set vivifies a fresh nested path as BLOCK containers [1]
cases.note: YAML seeds missing ancestors as bare `key:` (null), which `insertKey` promotes to a real block mapping — so a fresh nested path reads like hand-written YAML instead of a flow chain (`a: {b: {c: 1}}`).
